text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian airline operators will soon be charged higher fees to use local airports, as part of measures to give the airports financial autonomy.
- A total of 135,000 barrels of crude oil was lost during the shutdown of 12 Shell flow stations after a fire on Friday. The company said the flow stations were now back in operation.
- The Daily Times is not on the verge of bankruptcy, says administrator Peter Enahoro.
- Nigerian Ports Authority embarks on rehabilitation of some of its deteriorating facilities at the Apapa Ports Complex in Lagos.
- State-owned National Insurance Company of Nigeria (NICON) acquires Nigeria-Arab Bank after a successful takeover bid. The development will involve a 1.3 billion naira capital injection by NICON.

- Nigerian Telecommunications has been ordered to give priority to members of the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN), banks, media houses and oil companies in reconnecting lines in the Ikeja business district, which were cut off by a fire at the telephone exchange last year.

- Okitipupa Oil Palm will soon embark on a drive to raise 200 million naira. The company hopes the fresh capital will increase productivity by paying for new tractors and refurbishment of the oil mill.
- United States embassy says it has received no request inviting the ambassador or any other staff for interrogation by Nigerian police over terrorist bombings.
- The Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture may soon merge with the MAN.
- Managing director of Union Bank asks central bank to divest from its 60 percent share in the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation, to increase the independence of the two bodies.
